draft.title: Inclined planes, wedges and screws
card: Inclined plane
A ramp is a sloping surface. It lets a load be raised using less force than lifting it straight up, but the load must travel a longer path.
Wedge
Two ramps placed back to back make a wedge, such as an axe head or a knife blade. Pushing it forward forces material apart to the sides.
Screw
A ramp wrapped around a rod makes a screw. The ramp forms the spiral thread. Turning the screw moves it along a long path for a small distance forward.
A gentler slope needs less force but a longer path. The load ends up at the same height either way.
draft.remember: Ramps, wedges and screws trade a longer path for less force.

a.q: Why is it easier to push a box up a long ramp than to lift it straight up onto a truck?
opts: The ramp needs less force over a longer path
The ramp needs less force over a shorter path
The ramp needs more force over a longer path
The ramp lowers the height the box must reach
a.why: A ramp spreads the work over a longer path, so each push can be smaller. It does not shorten the path or lower the height the box must reach, which stays the same.
a.clue: Think about what you give up to get a smaller force.

b.q: Sam uses a wood screw to join two planks. Which description of the screw's thread is correct?
opts: A ramp wrapped around a rod
Two ramps joined back to back
A lever turning about a fulcrum
A ramp that is straight and flat
b.why: The thread of a screw is a ramp wound around a central rod. Two ramps back to back describe a wedge, which is the most tempting wrong choice, as both are made from ramps.
b.clue: Picture the spiral thread unwound and laid flat.

wants.brief: A right-angled triangle labelled ramp, shown beside a rod with the same triangle wrapped around it as a spiral thread, labelled screw thread.
wants.why: It shows that a screw is a ramp wrapped around a rod.

a.best: The ramp needs less force over a longer path

b.best: A ramp wrapped around a rod

problems.detail: The clue says to picture the thread 'unwound and laid flat'. That describes a straight ramp, so it could steer students to the wrong option 'A ramp that is straight and flat' instead of the right one, 'A ramp wrapped around a rod'.
